newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA'S HULUDAO H1 NET SURGES 54 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: CHINA'S HULUDAO H1 NET SURGES 54 PERCENT.

text.p: Half year ended June 30, 1997 (in millions of yuan unless stated otherwise, against first-half 1996 figures)
Earnings per share 0.2479 yuan vs 0.2066 yuan
Net assets per share 3.54 yuan vs 2.01 yuan
Company name: Huludao Zinc Industry Co Ltd.
NOTE: The results, calculated under Chinese accounting standards, were published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times on Friday.
It did not clarify whether the results have been audited.
Trading in Huludao's A shares was suspended on Friday morning pending the announcement and would resume in the afternoon, the Shenzhen Stock Exchange said.
The company, based in the city of Huludao in northeastern Liaoning province, is the largest zinc smelter in Asia.
The company, which listed 90 million domestic A shares in Shenzhen in June 1997, has an annual production capacity of 330,000 tonnes of zinc ingots.
The firm holds 20 percent of China's zinc market and 2.5 percent of the world's market.
Huludao forecast net profits of 189.01 million yuan for 1997 against 146.60 million yuan in 1996 and 147.98 million yuan in the previous year calculated in Chinese standards.
The company, which also produces sulphuric acid, targeted sales of 2.66 billion yuan for this year, compared with 2.13 billion yuan in 1996 and 2.26 billion yuan a year earlier.
Huludao has a total of 410 million shares, made up by 261.70 million institutional shares, 58.30 million staff-held shares and 90 million A shares.
